format: One JSON object. Required: wispSpell (1), id (lowercase-dashes), name. Everything else is optional.
fields: "1.0.0" — bump it when you change a spell the user already has
["*"] or e.g. ["claude","codex"]: which harnesses its prompt rules, blocks and hooks apply to
{ project: [names|ids|paths], agent: [...], mode: [...] } scope for prompt rules, blocks and hooks

{ name: { wisp: "/path?query" } | { gh: [args], cwd?: "task", refresh?: seconds } } — fetched by wisp; script functions receive them as their first argument { name: value }. gh args may use {field} templates over the card's task (e.g. "{pr.number}").

[{ id?, slot, label, icon?, title?, badge?: { count: "<data>" } | { text: "{field}" } | { fn, with: [data] }, group?: "name" (float only: folds into one button), corner?: "bottom-left", when?: {hasPr, prState, state, status, agent, project, unread, hasBranch} (card slots), do }]

[{ slot: "card.head" | "launcher.chips" | "composer.chips", text: "{field} template" | fn: "<script fn>" (returns a string), with?: [data], tone?: good|bad|warn|info|neutral, icon?, title?, when?, do? }]

[{ id, title, icon?, as: dialog|drawer|feed|card, slot?: card.top|card.bottom (as card), data: [names], render: "<script fn>", refresh?: { every: seconds, on: [summary, finished] } }] — render returns an array of wisp presentation blocks (stats, chart, markdown, checklist, files, callout, steps, tree, flow, terminal, code, actions with url…, preview, map, app)

[{ type, doc: "one-line JSON example + when to use it", summary: "{field} template for text-only places", render: "<script fn>" }] — new presentation blocks agents can use; render(block) returns wisp blocks
{ "<part>": { style?: { cssProp: value }, props?: {...}, order?: [...] (card.head only) } }
{ hide: [parts], tokens: { "--accent": "#7c5cff" }, dark: { … tokens for dark mode } }
["text", { text, when }] — added to agents' system prompts while the spell is on
{ key: value } — wins over the user's setting while the spell is on (theme: "dark" keeps wisp dark)
[{ name, args?, hint?, do }] — /name in a follow-up box; {args} in do's text is what the user typed after it
[{ label, keywords?, icon?, key?, do }] — ⌘K items (key: a single key like "g" or "shift+g", only when no built-in uses it)

[{ on, if?, max?, do }] — on: turn.finished | turn.failed | session.started | session.waiting; if: { status, testsFailed, agent, project, hasPr, mode }; do: one of reply, done, archive, forLater, notify, webhook; max: times per task (default 1)
[{ name, prompt with {params}, agent?, mode? }] — saved prompts

[{ key, name, role?, avatar?, brief, cron?: "5-field cron" (empty: only when asked), on?: [finished | done | ci], mode?: plan|edits|auto, agent?, model?, effort?, parallel?: 1-5, kit?: [{ kind: skill|rules, name, description (skills), body }], team?: [{ crew: "<key of another member here>" } | { agent }] }] — crew members the spell brings (at most 10). They join paused; the user reviews each and picks its project (one that starts when CI fails needs one). The spell owns who they are: change them by bumping the version. Prefer mode plan for a reviewer or watcher

JS with `export function name(data, ctx) { return … }` functions. It runs in a sandbox with no network, no DOM and no wisp API: it can only compute and return values (blocks, strings, numbers, lists of links). To make something interactive, return an app block: { type: "app", title, html: "<style>…</style>…<script>…</script>", height?, fallback?: [blocks] }. wisp runs its html in a sandboxed frame with no network, themed by wisp's CSS variables (var(--ink), --surface, --line, --accent, …); in it, wisp.send(text) offers text for the user to send to the task as a follow-up, wisp.save(obj) / wisp.state keep its state. Make it work from 320px wide. ctx: { session } (the card's task summary, when there is one), { block } for agent blocks (the block is also the first argument).
templates: {field} in text, labels, links and gh args is filled from the card's task summary: id, title, state, status, agent, model, mode, project, branch, cwd, preview, pr.number, pr.url, pr.state, pr.checks …; in slash commands {args} too. Missing fields become empty.
